model_note.S:
cc: Burning urination without systemic symptoms

HPI: 29 yo f. Patient reports: The burning began 2 days ago. It burns at the urethra when I pass urine. There is no pain into my back or groin. It is a stinging burning sensation. The burning is 4/10 and I urinate about every hour. It happens with every urination. It started after intercourse but there was no injury. Drinking water makes the urine sting a little less. Urinating triggers it. I have increased fluids but taken no medicine. I had one bladder infection 3 years ago. It burns when I urinate. I need to go every hour. I get sudden urges to go. There is mild low abdominal pressure.

Patient perspective: Do I have a kidney infection?

PMH: No diabetes, kidney disease or immunosuppression.

PSH: No surgery or hospitalizations.

Meds: No daily medicines.

Allergies: Sulfonamide antibiotic caused hives.

SH: Never smoked tobacco. One alcoholic drink weekly. No recreational drugs. Graphic designer; lives with husband; one established partner; uses condoms; last menstrual period 2 weeks ago, pregnancy not suspected.

FH: Mother has hypertension; father and brother are healthy.

ROS: Urinary - Reports dysuria. Reports frequency. Reports urgency. Denies flank pain. General - Denies fever. Denies chills. Denies fatigue. Gastrointestinal - Denies nausea. Denies vomiting. Reports abdominal pain.
model_note.O:
Vitals: T 98.4 F oral, P 78 bpm, BP 116/72 mmHg, R 16 rpm, Pulse Ox 99% on room air, Ht 5' 7", Wt 165 lbs

General: Alert. Comfortable and well hydrated.

Heart: Regular rhythm without murmur.

Lungs: Clear breath sounds bilaterally.

Abd: Abdomen not distended. Bowel sounds present. Mild suprapubic tenderness. Tympanic over the examined quadrants. No tenderness with gentle bilateral costovertebral angle percussion.

Osteopathic: T10 paraspinal tissue texture change with mild tenderness on the right.

Skin: No visible rash on the inspected arms.
P: 1. Obtain urinalysis and assess pregnancy possibility and complicated-infection features; choose an appropriate lower-UTI antibiotic after allergy and local-resistance review, avoiding sulfonamides; explain hydration, expected improvement and warning signs; reassess in 48–72 hours if not improving and seek prompt care for fever, flank pain or vomiting.

2. Assess colicky pain and hematuria and obtain urinalysis; use renal imaging only when the clinical picture warrants it; explain urgent precautions for severe pain, fever or inability to urinate; arrange urology evaluation if obstruction or persistent stone symptoms are found.

3. Ask about new soaps, spermicides and local irritants; discontinue a suspected irritant and assess genital symptoms as appropriate; educate on avoiding the identified irritant and arrange reassessment within 48–72 hours; refer for persistent symptoms rather than labeling a UTI without evidence.

model_note.S:
cc: Burning urination without systemic symptoms

HPI: 29 yo f. Patient reports: The burning began 4 days ago. It burns at the urethra when I pass urine. There is no pain into my back or groin. It is a stinging burning sensation. The burning is 4/10 and I urinate about every hour. It happens with every urination. It started after intercourse but there was no injury. Drinking water makes the urine sting a little less. Urinating triggers it. I have increased fluids but taken no medicine. I had one bladder infection 3 years ago. It burns when I urinate. I need to go every hour. I get sudden urges to go. There is mild low abdominal pressure.

Patient perspective: Do I have a kidney infection?

PMH: No diabetes, kidney disease or immunosuppression.

PSH: No surgery or hospitalizations.

Meds: No daily medicines.

Allergies: Sulfonamide antibiotic caused hives.

SH: Never smoked tobacco. One alcoholic drink weekly. No recreational drugs. Graphic designer; lives with husband; one established partner; uses condoms; last menstrual period 2 weeks ago, pregnancy not suspected.

FH: Mother has hypertension; father and brother are healthy.

ROS: Urinary - Reports dysuria. Reports frequency. Reports urgency. Denies flank pain. General - Denies fever. Denies chills. Denies fatigue. Gastrointestinal - Denies nausea. Denies vomiting. Reports abdominal pain.
model_note.O:
Vitals: T 98.4 F oral, P 78 bpm, BP 116/72 mmHg, R 16 rpm, Pulse Ox 99% on room air, Ht 5' 7", Wt 165 lbs

General: Alert. Comfortable and well hydrated.

Heart: Regular rhythm without murmur.

Lungs: Clear breath sounds bilaterally.

Abd: Abdomen not distended. Bowel sounds present. Mild suprapubic tenderness. Tympanic over the examined quadrants. No tenderness with gentle bilateral costovertebral angle percussion.

Osteopathic: T10 paraspinal tissue texture change with mild tenderness on the right.

Skin: No visible rash on the inspected arms.
P: 1. Obtain urinalysis and assess pregnancy possibility and complicated-infection features; choose an appropriate lower-UTI antibiotic after allergy and local-resistance review, avoiding sulfonamides; explain hydration, expected improvement and warning signs; reassess in 48–72 hours if not improving and seek prompt care for fever, flank pain or vomiting.

2. Assess colicky pain and hematuria and obtain urinalysis; use renal imaging only when the clinical picture warrants it; explain urgent precautions for severe pain, fever or inability to urinate; arrange urology evaluation if obstruction or persistent stone symptoms are found.

3. Ask about new soaps, spermicides and local irritants; discontinue a suspected irritant and assess genital symptoms as appropriate; educate on avoiding the identified irritant and arrange reassessment within 48–72 hours; refer for persistent symptoms rather than labeling a UTI without evidence.
